Single flat anchor group 'inference': inference, AI inference, inference workload(s), inference demand, inference request(s)/traffic/capacity, model/serving workload/demand/capacity, token generation/volume/tokens generated/processed, AI agent(s)/agent workload(s), enterprise AI usage/application(s), production AI/model deployment. track_a_nvda_a102.root_cause_note: This is NOT B1-stance misclassification -- the deterministic relation/gate logic correctly rejected content that is genuinely non-supportive. The break is upstream: the bullish narrative was never surfaced by NVDA's research agents in this run.

track_a_amd_a102.closest_near_miss: fundamental_agent:claim:82 -- CODE-VERIFIED SEGMENT ANALYSIS: the claim splits (on ':'/','/'.') into 3 segments: (1) 'data center ai accelerators mi series gpus', (2) 'the massive revenue acceleration and margin expansion strongly suggest amd s instinct mi300 mi400 series ai accelerators are ramping rapidly', (3) 'competing with nvidia in the ai training inference market'. Segment 3 contains the A102 anchor 'inference' but its only verb is 'competing' -- NOT in the predicate vocabulary. Segment 2 contains the predicate 'ramping' -- but 'ramp'/'ramping' is ITSELF ABSENT from POSITIVE_PREDICATES (verified: evaluate_ai_alpha_gates('AMD inference demand is ramping rapidly.') returns A102 passed=False; the equivalent sentence with 'accelerating' instead of 'ramping' DOES pass). Even if 'ramping' were added to the predicate vocabulary, this specific claim would STILL fail because the inference anchor (segment 3) and the ramping predicate (segment 2) are in DIFFERENT clauses, and the gate requires same-segment co-location.
track_a_amd_a102.root_cause_classification: MIXED -- two independent, compounding factors: (1) AMD-A102-RESEARCH_GAP (primary): none of AMD's 8 real MI-series claims assert an inference-SPECIFIC demand/growth fact isolated from the bundled 'training/inference market' framing; the real external distinction (FP4-for-inference vs FP8-for-training) that made this genuinely STRONG_GOLD was never captured by AMD's own research agents. (2) AMD-A102-SEMANTIC_GAP (secondary, newly identified by this audit): the AI hard gate's POSITIVE_PREDICATES vocabulary is missing the common hardware/business term 'ramp'/'ramping' (and the nominal form 'acceleration'), which is a real, narrow, low-risk gap independent of the research question -- but fixing it alone would NOT flip claim:82 due to the separate clause-boundary issue.
track_a_amd_a102.correction_to_prior_audit: The prior Evidence Starvation audit characterized this as 'the gate rejects bundled training/inference claims' -- direct gate re-execution shows the actual mechanism is more specific: it is not a deliberate anti-bundling exclusion (the gate would happily admit a claim asserting both A101 AND A102 in the same sentence, per the semantic contract's own example #5), it is a predicate-vocabulary gap plus a clause-boundary separation specific to how this particular claim was phrased.
track_a_amd_a102.recoverability: MEDIUM_CONFIDENCE_RECOVERABLE -- primarily via research coverage improvement (an isolated, single-clause 'AMD inference demand increased' assertion would cleanly pass); a narrow predicate-vocabulary addition (Track A102 Option B) is a secondary, smaller lever that alone is insufficient for this specific claim.

sndk_a102_negative_control.conclusion: TRUE EVIDENCE VACUUM, not a qualification/ticker-specificity/entity problem. No design option proposed in this audit (entity/ticker-specificity fixes, A102 research-coverage improvements, or A102 semantic-gate adjustments) can possibly activate SNDK A102, because there is no claim content of any kind to newly qualify -- SNDK_A102_FALSE_POSITIVE_RISK is evaluated as LOW for every option in Sections 18-19 on this basis. SNDK A102 remains a v1 Gold miss and is NOT treated as a system-recovery target, consistent with the prior Gold Benchmark Validity Audit's REVIEW_CANDIDATE classification (thematic-association risk: SNDK's real driver is AI-driven STORAGE demand, better fitting A103, not the compute/inference-specific A102 mechanism).

first_incorrect_decision.stage: Alpha Mapping -- Pure-LLM Semantic Authority classifier (comqutor_alpha/structure_engine/alpha_mapper.py::_classify_alpha_with_llm, lines ~354-450+)
first_incorrect_decision.exact_mechanism: The deterministic candidate-scoring layer correctly found NO eligible candidate for this claim: eligible_candidates=[], deterministic_top_alpha=null, deterministic_match_status='no_match', and the A201 candidate_score itself has eligible=false with no positive keyword/factor match. However, the Pure-LLM Semantic Authority classifier -- documented in alpha_mapper.py as 'the ONLY source of the semantic Alpha result...unrestricted by deterministic candidate generation/eligibility/score threshold/AI hard gate' -- independently selected A201 (matched_alpha='A201', alpha_match_method='llm', reason='llm semantic classifier selected from full canonical taxonomy'), OVERRIDING the deterministic layer's correct rejection.
first_incorrect_decision.why_it_happened: The LLM's classification prompt asks it to select the best-fitting canonical Alpha from the FULL taxonomy based on thematic/topical resemblance ('Memory/storage' + rally language + semiconductor-adjacent sector framing loosely resembles 'Semiconductor Supercycle'), but the prompt and validation contract (comqutor_alpha/structure_engine/alpha_mapper.py::_classify_alpha_with_llm's validate_response) contain NO requirement that the claim be substantively ABOUT the run's own ticker/company -- it only validates that the selected_alpha_id is a member of the canonical taxonomy. There is no entity-ownership check anywhere in the Alpha Mapping stage.
first_incorrect_decision.downstream_consequence: matched_alpha='A201' then flows, unmodified, into the evidence-qualification pipeline (graph_builder/_gather_qualifying_evidence), which correctly marks the claim non-ticker-specific (so it does NOT falsely inflate ticker_specificity), but it STILL counts toward evidence_count, unique_evidence_count, distinct_supporting_agents, direction_consistency, and (most materially) agent_independence -- because none of those components check entity ownership, only ticker-specificity does.

A company_names-style fix (Track A Option A) is structurally inapplicable to QQQ.
etf_special_case.kept_separate: This audit does NOT propose fixing ETF semantics -- consistent with the task's instruction, this is flagged as a distinct P4 PRODUCT_MODEL_GAP requiring a constituent-holdings data source and a new RELATIONAL_TICKER_EVIDENCE classification category, not a company_names or entity-ownership veto fix.

shared_root_cause_analysis.question: Do MSFT's ticker-specificity false negative and AMD's cross-company false positive share one common weak entity-ownership model?
shared_root_cause_analysis.mechanism: Both trace to the SAME underlying absence: the system has NO formal entity/issuer-ownership model anywhere (no ticker-to-company-alias registry, no claim-level 'is this claim substantively about ticker X' classifier). But they manifest at TWO DIFFERENT, INDEPENDENT pipeline stages via TWO DIFFERENT mechanisms: MSFT's false negative occurs at the ACTIVATION stage's ticker-specificity check (_is_ticker_specific), which is too strict because it has no company-name data to check against -- an absence-of-check-input problem. AMD's false positive occurs at the ALPHA MAPPING stage's Pure-LLM matched_alpha assignment, which has no ownership check AT ALL (not even a strict one) -- an absence-of-check-existence problem, one full pipeline stage earlier. Fixing MSFT's problem (populating company_names) does nothing for AMD's, because AMD's contamination is decided before ticker-specificity is ever evaluated. This is why the task's Section 20 instruction to not force one unified fix is correct: these are two real, separate defects that happen to share a root THEME (weak entity modeling) but require two separate, independently-sequenced fixes.
